recipes.name: Black Bean Salad
ingredients_raw: 1 (15 ounce) can black beans, rinsed and drained
2 (15 ounce) cans whole kernel corn, drained

steps.text: In a large bowl, combine the black beans, corn, green onions, jalapeno peppers, bell pepper, avocado, pimentos, tomatoes, cilantro, lime juice, and Italian dressing. Season with garlic salt. Toss, and chill until serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Black Bean Salad
raw_recipe.description: This salad is a kaleidoscope of color and taste - black beans, yellow corn, green peppers, and red, red tomatoes. Lime juice, garlic and jalapeno give it some punch.

review.reviewBody: I am not quite sure why the 1 user didn't care for this dish. I made the mistake of fixing it last night for a mexican theme tonight. Now I have to fix another bowl today because there is only about a cup left. This is such an easy recipe and it does NOT have to be followed by the letter to turn out grand.....Be creative...

This is my 'go to' salad for soup/salad luncheons, especially when chili is served. I'm lucky enough to have corn fresh-frozen from the family garden, which is better than canned. I normally add at least one more avocado, as the dressing keeps the avocado chunks nice and green. This salad is also great as a dip for corn chip "scoopers", and I think I like it even better that way - the salt from the chip enhances the veggie mixture. If I were to make this for our small family, I think I would cut everything in half except for the black beans - otherwise, it makes a large amount (although it stores well in the frig).

This was excellent. The changes I made are to first DRAIN AND RINSE THE BEANS. The first time I made it I did not and it got sloppy and mushy. I used frozen white shoepeg corn, only because I personally hate canned corn (if you use canned I'd drain that too), and I used one can black beans and one can kidneys - just to add to the color. Also, instead of bottled Italian dressing I made my own with capers, caper juice, white wine, balsamic vinegar, olive oil, and garlic - you can probably use any kind of oil/vinegar dressing you like. The jalepeno added just enough spice, I'd personally use a little more but this was fine. Oh - and I used whole grape tomatoes, sliced ones may make it too runny also.

Made this for a family gathering today. I did follow a lot of other review suggestions. In the end I used 2 cans of black beans rinsed well, 1 can of corn, 1 cup of Trader Joes frozen roasted corn defrosted, 2 cans of diced tomatoes w/chilies, a little over half a red onion diced, zest and juice of 1 lime, 1/2 cup chopped cilantro, about 6 diced red/yellow/orange mini sweet peppers, 1/2 cup of italian dressing and salt and pepper tom taste. I also used a few dashes of Goya Adobo seasoning and some grinds from a tex mex chipotle spice blend. I made it first thing in the morning and let it chill until about 1 pm. We ate it around 2pm with tortilla chips. We grazed it the rest of the day. Everyone seemed to enjoy it. Thanks for posting this recipe. Can't wait until I can try it with grilled chicken or with pasta.

I served this as a topping for a lettuce (iceberg/romaine combo) salad. I topped the bean mixture with Mexican Shredded Cheese. This was a big hit at a Mexican Pot Luck. I think the lime juice really gives it a nice flavor. I only used one can of corn and that was perfect for me. I think two would have been too much. My avocado was not quite ripe, so I did not have the problem others did who said it turned to mush. Mine stayed firm. I only used 1/4 cup of salad dressing, and might skip altogether next time. I didn't have garlic salt, so used 1/4 tsp. salt and 1/4 tsp. garlic powder. I think maybe minced or roasted garlic would be a nice touch. This is a very nice, versatile recipe. Thanks for sharing.

subbed canned green chilis for pimentos & served guacamole & jalapenos on side to be added according to taste. 
saved in favorites.
I added fresh garlic cloves and more cilantro, & double the recipe ????????????it’s definitely a 10 on the taste scale

This has become a staple in our house. I have always used an orange pepper in place of green (just don't like green ones). I LOVE black beans so I use 2 cans of beans and only one of corn. I also cut the tomatoes and remove the seeds and goop first, so it doesn't get soggy. I've never taken it anywhere and not had someone ask me for the recipe. Delicious!

My whole family loved this! I first had it when visiting a friend clear across the country, and asked her for the recipe. She made a copy for me and I had to smile when I read that it was from Allrecipes, my favorite recipe source. One daughter does not like black beans, corn, or tomatoes and was hesitant to try it, but then raved about the combination. Following my friend's example, I added cubed pepper jack cheese, but then was concerned it may be too hot for my kids with the jalapenos, so left them out. Next time I will probably add jalapenos from my garden and use Monterey Jack cheese. I didn't have a lime so used a small lemon. I used garlic powder and sea salt instead of garlic salt, and no pimentos, minor changes. Our power was out, so it was perfect to fix by flashlight! Due to that, I just served it with tortilla chips. I couldn't stop eating it, it was great! Thank you!

I have made this salad a number of times. I love the leftovers. I usually wait and add the avocado to the portion I am serving. It is huge so I half the recipe and have used canned jalapeno peppers and red, orange or yellow peppers according to whats on sale.
I made it with fewer beans (one can) and two avocados. It was a really big hit at our Fajita night!

This one will be on repeat. Perfect to up my fiber and protein. Only changes: used yellow bell pepper (for color & sweetness), 2 avocados, heirloom cherry tomatoes (cut in 1/2) and Olive Garden's Zesty Italian Dressing. So flavorful!
I didn't have any fresh tomatoes. I used canned fire roasted tomatoes and drained them. Wonderful flavor.
Added flaked tuna or chicken
Absolutely delicious. Rather than using bottle dressing I made a Mexican cilantro vinegarette dressing. This recipe would be great for a pot luck!
I made this several times over the last 2 years and everyone loved it. I am not great in the kitchen and this is easy and wonderful!
Great as a side dish or a dip with tortilla chips.

I thought it was very good and hubby thought it was excellent after having three servings. Followed the recipe pretty much as written, had to sub chopped onions for green onions. Contained all ingredients we like so - what’s not to like. Served as a side for grilled chicken tacos. It was very flavorful. Can’t speak to how it is the next day, as we ate it all in one night. Will definitely make again. The mix of pimentos. Italian dressing, lime juice had me a little apprehensive but decided to go with it , so glad we did!!

Very good as written with the Italian twist to it. It’s also very similar to a family fav with a few substitutions. Instead of Italian dressing use your favorite Mexican tomato salsa, hot or mild as you like. We also put in diced green chilies and/or jalapeños rather than bell pepper. Nice addition also is sliced green onions and grape or cherry tomatoes. It makes a great party dip with tortilla chips!

So beautiful & delicious! Good by itself, on nachos, baked potato, pulled pork ... anything! Even better as leftovers as flavors blend:). The second time I made I thought more lime juice would be better ... I was wrong. Juice from one small lime is all that’s needed. Enjoy!
